llm.summary: The skill’s Kia vehicle access purpose is coherent, but it should be reviewed because it runs an unpinned external MCP package with plaintext Kia credentials and default vehicle command capability.

dimensions.detail: The setup example places Kia username and password values directly in project or user MCP configuration while the server can read sensitive vehicle data and, by default, register climate and charging commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses `npx -y kiaaccess-mcp` without a pinned version or integrity control, so mutable external code is downloaded and executed with the supplied account credentials.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger wording is broad, but the artifact repeatedly requires user confirmation for commands, warns not to guess vehicle keys, and describes dry-run behavior when confirm is absent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly discloses local remember-me token persistence, token export sensitivity, and a confirm-gated forget-session tool, though users should treat the stored token as a durable MFA bypass.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented tools match the stated Kia Access purpose: vehicle status, location, EV charge data, and confirm-gated climate, charging, lock, and unlock commands using the user’s own account.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Only install this if you trust the `kiaaccess-mcp` package and are comfortable giving it Kia account access. Prefer a pinned reviewed package version, keep real credentials out of project files, set `KIA_WRITE_MODE=none` unless commands are needed, and protect or revoke any exported remember-me token like a password.
llm.findings:
[AS2] unexpected: Kia authentication is necessary for the integration, but the artifact-backed setup stores high-value account credentials in `.mcp.json`, including a project-level option, without safer secret-storage guidance.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Kia-request trigger fits the skill’s purpose, and command tools are documented as confirm-gated, so this is a caution rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
[T08] unexpected: Using an MCP package is purpose-aligned, but automatic unpinned `npx -y` execution is not required and materially increases supply-chain risk for a credentialed vehicle-control integration.
[T09] unexpected: Plaintext credential configuration is documented in the artifact and is a real concern because the same account can expose vehicle information and command capability.
